drafts.stack: The new particle driver allocates one slice-index array per particle. The patch places this buffer on the stack when NS is at most 512 and keeps heap allocation for larger arrays. Direct calls to the compiled driver reached the slice declaration and then removed an out-of-domain particle. Median heap allocation over seven rounds was 32 to 0 bytes at NS=1, 64 to 0 at NS=9, 2,072 to 0 at NS=512, and 2,080 to 2,080 at NS=513. Complete simulation runtime was not measured.
drafts.vertical: Repeated searches at the same finite height can reuse the previous layer index while HOKART and NKK are unchanged. Searches at changed heights still run the existing binary search and add cache bookkeeping. In the original 45 cases, all 15 constant-height cases were faster, while 29 of the 30 cases with changing heights were slower. Two synthetic terrain projects recorded 444,724 reused results in 889,446 cached calls, about 50%. A separate synthetic paired benchmark with a 50% repeat fraction was faster in all 18 cases, by 1.148 to 1.585 times. These inputs do not replay Main height traces. Timing includes a fresh cache for each particle and measures lookup cost only; full GRAL speedup was not measured.

final_captions.stack: Each new particle allocates a heap array for concentration slice indices. The patch uses the stack for NS <= 512 and keeps the heap fallback above that limit. In direct calls to the compiled driver, median allocation fell from 32 to 0 bytes at NS=1, from 64 to 0 at NS=9, and from 2,072 to 0 at NS=512. At NS=513, both versions allocated 2,080 bytes. The calls reached the slice declaration and then removed an out-of-domain particle, so these numbers describe allocation at that entry point. Complete simulation runtime was not measured.

All 15 constant-height cases in the original benchmark were faster; 29 of the 30 cases with changing heights were slower. Two synthetic terrain projects recorded 444,724 reused results in 889,446 cached calls, about 50%. A separate benchmark with paired heights and a 50% repeat fraction was faster in all 18 cases, by 1.148 to 1.585 times. Those sequences are synthetic and do not replay Main height traces. Timings include a fresh cache for each particle and report lookup cost only. Full GRAL speedup was not measured.
